Run command-center/tests/test_owner_report.py with run_tests: your new test must fail for the reason you describe, every other test in the file must still pass. +++ b/command-center/tests/test_owner_report.py
@@ -100,3 +100,31 @@ def test_main_reads_a_file_and_dry_runs(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
     assert orp.main(["--file", str(report)]) == 0
     assert "DRY RUN" in capsys.readouterr().out
     assert orp.main(["--file", str(tmp_path / "missing.md")]) == orp.EXIT_USAGE
+
+
+def test_send_report_does_not_raise_on_close_failure_after_send_failure(monkeypatch):
+    """If transport.send fails and transport.close also raises, send_report should still return an error dict, not raise."""
+    _configured(monkeypatch)
+    class FailingTransport:
+        def __init__(self, settings):
+            self.settings = settings
+            self.sent = []
+            self.closed = False
+        async def send(self, person, text, **kw):
+            # Simulate a delivery failure on the first attempt
+            raise RuntimeError("send failed")
+        async def close(self):
+            # Simulate a failure during close
+            raise RuntimeError("close failed")
+
+    def factory(settings):
+        return FailingTransport(settings)
+
+    text = "some report text"
+    # This should not raise; it should return an error dict about send failure.
+    result = asyncio.run(orp.send_report(text, send=True, transport_factory=factory))
+    # Expect an error dict for send failure
+    assert result["exit"] == orp.EXIT_SEND_FAILED
+    assert result["ok"] is False
+    assert "delivery failed" in result["reason"]
+    # Ensure no exception was propagated (if close raised, we would have gotten an exception)
